COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
IA No.11 of 2024 (Compounding Application)
in
C482 No.778 of 2020
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. R. P. Nautiyal, learned Senior
Counsel, assisted by Ms. Garima Singh,
learned counsel for the applicants.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief
Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Veer Kunwar Singh, learned
counsel for the private respondent.
4. The present Petition has been preferred
under Section 482 Cr.P.C., along with a
Compounding Application supported with the
affidavits of all the applicants and the
respondent-complainant. All the applicants
and the respondent-complainant are present
in the Court and are identified by their
respective counsels through their Adhar Card
and copies of the same are kept on record.
5. The brief facts of the case are that the
applicant no. 3 married with respondent no.2
on 18.11.2018 and there is no issue from this
marriage, however, due to some differences
they are living separately since 09.10.2019.
6. On the previous date, i.e., 22.05.2024,
counsel for both the parties submitted that
parties have settled their disputes to get
divorce by mutual consent under section 13-
B of the Hindu Marriage Act, and it has also
been decided that the husband will pay a
sum of Rupees 15 lacs to the wife towards
permanent alimony, out of which, Rupees 5
lacs has already been paid. Thereafter, the
matter was listed on 6th of June, 2024, and
on that date, the husband of the respondent-complainant agreed to pay the remaining
amount and simultaneously a liberty was
given to the applicants to move an application
for waiver of statuary period as provided

2024:UHC:5957
under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage
Act, before the Court. In compliance to the
liberty given by this Court vide order dated
06.06.2024, an application was moved by
both the parties before the Judge, Family
Court, Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar
for waiver of the statuary period, however, the
Judge, Family Court posted the matter on
24th October, 2024.
7. Learned counsel for the parties submit
that if the parties have settled their disputes
to get divorce by mutual consent, the Law is
very well settled that the statuary period
should be waived of.

8. I have perused the order passed by the
Judge, Family Court, Kashipur, dated
02.07.2024, and in opinion of this Court
since the parties have settled their disputes
and today the husband of the respondent-complainant submits that he will pay the rest
of the amount within a week, then in such
eventuality the Judge, Family Court,
Kashipur should preponed the matter for
waiver of the statutory period of notice so that
the divorce decree be passed as early as
possible.
9. Mr. R. P. Nautiyal, learned Senior
Advocate submits that the husband of the
respondent-complainant is serving in
Merchant Navy and he has to leave to join the
job.
10. Since the parties have decided to get
divorce by mutual consent and, for which,
they have already proceeded and the part
payment towards the permanent alimony has
already been paid and today the husband of
the complainant undertakes before this Court
that he will pay the entire remaining amount
of the alimony within a week from today and
this Court also interacts with the respondent-complainant, who submits that the
proceedings be dropped as they have settled
their disputes.
11. The State counsel Mr. Pratiroop Pande,

2024:UHC:5957
submits that since the dispute is relating to
the matrimonial, therefore, there will be no
useful purpose to continue the proceedings
and the compounding application may be
allowed.
12. Accordingly, the Compounding
Application is allowed. The summoning order
dated 20.07.2020 and the further
proceedings of Case Crime No. 38 of 2020
and Criminal Case No. 550 of 2020, under
Sections 498-A, 504, 506 of IPC and Sections
3⁄4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, PS Bazpur,
District Udham Singh Nagar, pending in the
Court of Judicial Magistrate, Bazpur, District
Udham Singh Nagar are quashed.

13. Apart from this, both the parties are
directed to move immediately an application
before the Judge, Family Court, where the
petition under Section 13-B is pending for
adjudication to pre-pone the date and if such
an application is moved, the Judge, Family
Court, Kashipur is directed to pre-pone the
matter and to decide the Section 13-B
Petition as early as possible so that the
husband of respondent-complainant may
leave to join his job.
14. Subject to the above, present C-482
Petition stands disposed of.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 22.08.2024
Kaushal
